title: I Used To Have A Cat

segments.text: Wait. I used to have a cat.
segments.acting_note: Eyes dart from off-screen straight into camera lens. 2-frame blink. Forward lean.

segments.text: Okay—not like that. I didn't buy one.
segments.acting_note: Both palms up in a quick defensive shrug. Asymmetric eyebrow arch.

segments.text: I found her abandoned behind a row of mailboxes.
segments.acting_note: Eye shift to upper right recalling memory, pointing gesture.

segments.text: She was tiny. Like, fit-in-my-pocket tiny.
segments.acting_note: Holding fingers a couple inches apart, soft empathetic brow raise.

segments.text: Just sitting inside a damp cardboard box, shivering.
segments.acting_note: Leaning down, gaze down-right toward cardboard box, sympathetic eye softening.

segments.text: So naturally, I brought her a little bowl of warm milk.
segments.acting_note: Sliding milk bowl forward gently, open palm invitation.

segments.text: At first, she hissed at my shoelaces.
segments.acting_note: Half-smirk, eyebrow cocked, glance down at shoes.

segments.text: But ten minutes later? Purring like a tiny lawnmower.
segments.acting_note: Warm fond smile, hand on chest, soft blush.

segments.text: I wanted to keep her so badly.
segments.acting_note: Hands clutched together, earnest pleading eyes directly to camera.

segments.text: Then my parents took one look and said: absolutely not.
segments.acting_note: Instant 0-frame posture drop. Straight horizontal dash mouth. Total freeze for 0.8s.

segments.text: I couldn't just leave her outside.
So I convinced the corner shopkeeper to let her stay behind the counter.
segments.acting_note: Pointing to shop counter cutaway, explanatory gesture.

segments.text: And for four days, she basically ran the register.
segments.acting_note: Smug smile, chuckling side glance toward Neeko on counter.

segments.text: Meanwhile, I was texting everyone I knew, putting up little drawings...
segments.acting_note: Phone prop in left hand, tapping screen, doodle posters popping up.

segments.text: and asking every single customer who walked into the shop.
segments.acting_note: Counting fingers, earnest persistence, slight laugh.

segments.text: And on Friday... this really lovely family came in and adopted her on the spot.
segments.acting_note: Warm radiant smile, relaxed posture, fond eyes.
Soft heartfelt pause, head tilts gently, sincere warmth.

segments.text: I still think about her sometimes.
segments.acting_note: Looking slightly up, reflective, fond smile.

segments.text: I'm just really glad I got to help.
segments.acting_note: Direct eye contact with viewer, gentle nod, soft smile into fade.
